# Performance scoreboard

Every hot path and resource metric of PiG, with its current count, the ratchet gate that guards it, a target and its basis, and the owning lane. Pi-identical output is the wall: a change that lowers a count must keep every parity test green.

Counts do not depend on machine speed (allocations, bytes, GC cycles, goroutines, descriptors, children, sizes). Time is measured only on the benchmark cluster with the exact-CV gate and is not recorded here. Ceilings live in `automation/perf/ratchet.toml` and only move down (`make perf-ratchet-check`).

Measured at `4198d7fae7+changes` with go1.27.2 on linux/amd64 by `make perf-scoreboard-measure`.

40 metrics; 242 gates: 214 in this tree, 4 on another lane's branch, 24 missing.

| Area | Metric | Status | Impact | Owner | Target | Gates and current counts |
|---|---|---|---:|---|---|---|

## Cross-language comparison method

Every comparison with another harness follows this protocol. Targets that cite another harness's self-reported numbers stand only until a same-machine run replaces them.

Harnesses: pi_agent_rust v0.6.1 (a Rust port of Pi; run first); PiG (stock, default and PGO builds); rpi (Rust port of Pi; default and tuned release builds); Pi 1.3.0 (Node); Codex CLI.

Platforms: Linux, bare metal; Windows 11.

Endpoints:

- --version: exec to exit
- spawn to the first answered RPC command
- first frame in a PTY
- first accepted input in a PTY
- RSS and PSS at ready (rpi's metric), beside peak RSS

Scenarios:

- startup (every endpoint above)
- harness-only overhead over 100 and 1,000 turns against a scripted mock
- long sessions at 1M, 2M and 3M tokens: resume and per-turn cost
- token forwarding latency, open loop, p50 to p99.9, no coordinated omission
- extension round trip per SDK (Go, Rust, Python, TypeScript)
- sessions per host, N = 1 to 1,000
- worker cold start (deployed startup_time_ms)
- reliability: seeded faults, kill-and-resume pass rate with a Wilson interval, orphans, leak slope, cancel latency
- 24-hour scripted soak: goroutines (goroutineleak profile), descriptors and children sampled every minute, gated flat, published beside CPU
- render path: GC pause and mark-assist histograms over 10,000 keystrokes

Rules:

- One machine for every harness; never compare numbers from different machines or published self-reports as a ranking.
- Bare metal, CPU governor performance, turbo off, isolated cores, ASLR on, a fresh process per run.
- Twenty runs per harness, interleaved in an order fixed in advance; report the ratio of medians with a bootstrap interval at 95 percent confidence, an A/A noise floor, and an equivalence margin declared before the run.
- A scripted mock provider with a fixed chunk schedule runs outside the harness's cgroup; every harness gets an isolated HOME.
- Builds 2x2: Rust default and tuned, Go default and PGO; each competitor is built with its own release flags (Rust LTO and PGO, Go -s -w and PGO).
- Process timing with hyperfine 2.0 --shell=none (memory_peak_resident and instruction counters recorded, not ranked).
- Noise control from the LLVM benchmarking list: performance governor, shielded CPUs, SMT siblings off, turbo off, no swap (a swapped GC metadata page faults into a pause).
- On Kubernetes: CPU Manager static policy, Guaranteed QoS, full-pcpus-only, one benchmark pod per node.
- Reporting (Heiser's benchmarking crimes): every sub-benchmark including losses, geometric means over sub-benchmarks, absolute numbers beside every ratio.
